pull.title: [wip,nomerge,rfc] build: Require C++23 compiler
pull.body:
C++23 for Bitcoin Core is mostly a "style update" on top of C++20. However, the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes (https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/commit/bdd0cd69418d189f62699d274a751cbf6d36bb43).

I don't know when it is fine to switch, but at some point, I think it is fine to require a C++23 compiler, so that [new stuff](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34979#issuecomment-4448399166) is unlocked. Of course this requires bumping the minimum required compiler versions:

* GCC: 13
* Clang: 19

There are some C++23 features that aren't implemented (such as `<stacktrace>` not really shipped in any vanilla stdlib today), or e.g. `ranges::starts_with` not implemented until libstdc++-16. But overall I think we are better off using C++23 without those few features instead of waiting longer?

> iwyu incorrectly suggests to remove the util/expected include

This looks like IWYU's ["Automatic re-export: function return values"](https://github.com/include-what-you-use/include-what-you-use/blob/master/docs/WhatIsAUse.md#automatic-re-export-function-return-values) heuristics in action.

My inline comments cover build and IPC compatibility, the skipped-path regression in block import, test guards for `expected`, and optional C++23 cleanups.

I have added patches to illustrate those suggestions, but I don't think we should fix them all here - but it would make sense to add a small compile sample for each to demonstrate support across our infrastructure - then handle the exhaustive call-site migrations in separate PRs.

events.message:
test: Adjust util::Expected tests for C++23

1) value() might be marked [[nodiscard]], so add the missing (void),
   where the value is ignored.

2) std::expected::value() must be able to throw
   std::bad_expected_access<E> if the expected contains an error. That
   requires copying the error type, which is not possible in this unit
   test that uses a non-copyable error type.

   Fix it by using the non-throwing value accessor.

> [aa80723](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36033/changes/aa80723e89ee10a95c3b5dac949d97d4fe07efce) _build: Require C++23 compiler_:

Cap'n Proto 0.9.2 headers fail with GCC 14 and Apple Clang in C++23. The libmultiprocess compatibility check could be updated separately to cover C++23. Here, requiring Cap'n Proto 1.0 when IPC is enabled would cover bundled and external libmultiprocess builds.

<details><summary>Example patch</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index a48902d3c3..7b67b25fd4 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -256,6 +256,11 @@ if(WITH_ZMQ)
   find_package(ZeroMQ 4.0.0 MODULE REQUIRED)
 endif()
 
+if(ENABLE_IPC)
+  # Older Cap'n Proto headers fail with compilers that implement P2468R2.
+  find_package(CapnProto 1.0 CONFIG REQUIRED)
+endif()
+
 if(ENABLE_IPC AND WITH_EXTERNAL_LIBMULTIPROCESS)
   find_package(Libmultiprocess REQUIRED COMPONENTS Lib)
   find_package(LibmultiprocessNative REQUIRED COMPONENTS Bin
diff --git a/doc/dependencies.md b/doc/dependencies.md
index a0f71f579b..5e2a282b4e 100644
--- a/doc/dependencies.md
+++ b/doc/dependencies.md
@@ -37,7 +37,7 @@ with support for C++23 features including std::byteswap and std::views::zip.
 
 | Dependency | Releases | Minimum required |
 | --- | --- | --- |
-| [Cap'n Proto](../depends/packages/native_capnp.mk) ([IPC](multiprocess.md)) | [link](https://capnproto.org/) | [0.9.2](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36747) (1.0 with Clang) |
+| [Cap'n Proto](../depends/packages/native_capnp.mk) ([IPC](multiprocess.md)) | [link](https://capnproto.org/) | [1.0](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36033) |
 | [libmultiprocess](../depends/packages/native_libmultiprocess.mk) ([IPC](multiprocess.md)) | [link](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/tags) | [v14.0](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36817) |
 | Python (scripts, tests) | [link](https://www.python.org) | [3.10](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/30527) |
 | [Qt](../depends/packages/qt.mk) (gui) | [link](https://download.qt.io/archive/qt/) | [6.2](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/30997) |
```
</details>

> [cf8e2c6](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36033/changes/cf8e2c6bfe496665edecfb293b9838c5398d6027) _refactor: clang-tidy readability-container-contains for C++23_:

We already compile the bundled libmultiprocess as C++23. Its standalone build still supports C++20, so changing those tests to `.contains()` here would break it. Could the tidy job disable only `readability-container-contains` for the subtree?

> [aa80723](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36033/changes/aa80723e89ee10a95c3b5dac949d97d4fe07efce) _build: Require C++23 compiler_:

The RISC-V link test still compiles and links its internal-header consumer as C++20. I'd update both flags to C++23 for this migration.

<details><summary>Example patch</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/ci/test/link-riscv.sh b/ci/test/link-riscv.sh
index 93bebfa8a9..bba7d5f1a9 100755
--- a/ci/test/link-riscv.sh
+++ b/ci/test/link-riscv.sh
@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@ LIBM=$("${GCC}" -print-file-name=libm.a)
 
 echo -e "#include <script/script_error.h>\n int main() { return ScriptErrorString(ScriptError_t::SCRIPT_ERR_UNKNOWN_ERROR).size() > 0; }" > test.cpp
 
-"${GXX}" -I "${BASE_ROOT_DIR}"/src -g -std=c++20 -c test.cpp -o test.o
+"${GXX}" -I "${BASE_ROOT_DIR}"/src -g -std=c++23 -c test.cpp -o test.o
 
 # Make the binary executable on linux for testing purposes
 echo -e ".section .text
@@ -52,7 +52,7 @@ echo -e "#include <sys/stat.h>
 
 "${GCC}" -g -c syscalls.c -o syscalls.o
 
-"${GXX}" -g -std=c++20 \
+"${GXX}" -g -std=c++23 \
     -nostdlib \
     "${CRTBEGIN}" \
     test.o \
```
</details>
